H2OK04055.name: Tom Cole
H2OK04055.bio: U.S. Representative and Chairman of the House Appropriations Committee; former Oklahoma Secretary of State, state senator, small business owner and college instructor.

positions.stance: Supports the SAVE Act, saying "every American should feel secure about our elections system," including a nationwide voter ID requirement.
Says he has "been proud to stand strong for our second amendment rights" and fights the far left's agenda on guns in the House.
Works to protect Oklahoma's military installations from cuts and to add missions, stressing the state's role in keeping the nation safe.
Fought to end the oil export ban and "continues to fight for American Energy Independence and Oklahoma's economy."
Has "always fought to protect the unborn," citing a 100% National Right to Life rating and an A+ from Susan B. Anthony List.

H6OK04155.name: Mitchell Jacob
H6OK04155.bio: U.S. Army veteran and former cryptologic linguist, former stockbroker, banker and mortgage loan originator, now working as a public defender.

positions.stance: Pledges to uphold "individual liberty and justice for all," calling individual rights and the rule of law the minimum requirements for public office.
"We need to stop raising the debt limit, cut spending, and eliminate the federal debt."
Says public schools "should be funded and provide free meals" and that every child deserves a quality education.
"I do not accept PAC money." Describes a grassroots campaign of individual donors and volunteers.
Wants work visas, asylum claims and refugee requests processed fairly and swiftly, and opposes masked agents and "inhumane camps."

H0OK05205.name: Stephanie Bice
H0OK05205.bio: U.S. Representative for Oklahoma's Fifth Congressional District, serving her third term, with private-sector and state legislative experience.

positions.stance: Authored the Protecting Military Veteran Families with Disabilities Act and backs expanded veteran access to healthcare, job training and education benefits.
Committed to "maintaining order at the southern border"; supports common-sense immigration reforms and stronger enforcement.
Supports protecting free speech, religious liberty and due process, and is "a strong defender of the Second Amendment."
Working to "rein in Washington's out-of-control spending," eliminate duplicative grant programs, and root out waste, fraud and abuse.
Supports Oklahoma's oil and gas industry and opposes regulations that threaten domestic energy production and American jobs.

H6OK05293.name: Jena Nelson
H6OK05293.bio: Nonprofit development professional, corporate leadership developer and small business owner; former educator and 2020 Oklahoma Teacher of the Year.

positions.stance: Opposes the "big beautiful bill," saying it adds $2.4 trillion to the deficit and leaves millions more uninsured to fund tax breaks for the wealthy.
Pledges to protect and strengthen Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid, expand Medicare drug price negotiation, and fight fraud without cutting benefits.
Supports more border agents and technology, faster asylum decisions, and more work visas, saying "a secure border and a fair immigration system aren't opposites."
Opposes cuts to the VA and pledges to "improve healthcare for our bravest men and women."
Supports capping insulin costs, expanding SNAP and free school meals, a $17 minimum wage, and an expanded Child Tax Credit.

H6CT01206.name: Luke Bronin
H6CT01206.bio: Former mayor of Hartford, Connecticut, from 2016 to 2024.

positions.stance: Pledges to "focus relentlessly to make life easier and more affordable," citing housing, healthcare, electricity, groceries, childcare and eldercare.
Proposes stopping ICE's "lawlessness" in the short term while working to abolish ICE and rebuild the immigration system.
Wants to protect Medicare and Medicaid, negotiate down prescription drug prices, and "push for universal, affordable healthcare."
Says making the federal government "get serious about housing" will be one of his top priorities.
Says care should be treated "as essential and worthy of fair pay" as childcare and eldercare costs squeeze families.

H2CT03102.name: Amy Chai
H2CT03102.bio: Physician specializing in primary care and addiction medicine.

positions.stance: Says the middle class is struggling and that "good character and hard work should guarantee the security of a home and family."
A physician who says a few "laser-targeted laws could substantially reduce costs nationwide" and wants to focus on preventing chronic illness.
"Parents have every right to determine what their children are learning, whether it be through public schools or home education."
Supports up-front investment in preventing mental illness and addiction, arguing prevention saves lives and taxpayer money.
Says "We must spend less"; supports capping property taxes, eliminating the self-employment tax, and shifting taxes from earned income to the financial industry.

H2CT02112.name: Joe Courtney
H2CT02112.bio: U.S. Representative for eastern Connecticut since 2006; former public defender and private-practice attorney.

positions.stance: Supports investing in roads, bridges, rail and transit, calling infrastructure investment "about good jobs and growing our economy."
Calls agriculture "a critical component of our region's economy" and has made supporting the district's farmers a top priority.
"Every American deserves access to quality, timely, and affordable health care"; fighting to lower costs and support the health care workforce.
Backs the region's submarine industry, from the Groton shipyard to suppliers across the district, as "the submarine capital of the world."
Says quality, affordable education is "the key to a thriving and growing middle class"; supports investment in higher education and workforce training.

H6CT02196.name: George Austin
H6CT02196.bio: Small business owner with a degree in construction management from Central Connecticut State University.

positions.stance: Pledges to work with local leaders "to make life affordable again"; criticizes the extended state corporate tax surcharge.
Wants federal funds directed toward apprenticeships, job training and technical education connected with local employers like defense manufacturers.
Supports stronger border security, a faster and stricter asylum process, and replacing catch-and-release with consistent processing, while expanding legal ports of entry.

H0CT03072.name: Rosa DeLauro
H0CT03072.bio: U.S. Representative for Connecticut's 3rd District since 1991 and Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Committee.

positions.stance: Supports making the expanded Child Tax Credit permanent, Medicare drug price negotiation, and an economy "built from the middle out, not the top down."
"Everyone should have affordable healthcare"; supports strengthening the ACA, Medicare and Medicaid, and codifying Roe v. Wade protections.
Calls public schools "the heart of our communities" and fights to deliver federal resources, including Title I and disability funding, to schools.
Calls Social Security and Medicare "earned benefits" and opposes any attempt to cut them, raise the retirement age, or privatize Medicare.
Supports a permanent expanded Child Tax Credit, lower child care costs, and "a national paid family leave program."

H6CT03178.name: Christopher Lancia
H6CT03178.bio: U.S. Coast Guard veteran and former federal law enforcement officer who works as an OSP manager at a fiber network provider.

positions.stance: "Fight inflation, lower taxes, and hold Washington accountable for reckless spending."
"We must control our borders to stop the flow of drugs and crime into our towns."
"Parents—not bureaucrats—should make decisions for their children. Schools should focus on academics, not agendas."
"Push for term limits and restore accountability in government."

H8CT04172.name: Jim Himes
H8CT04172.bio: U.S. Representative from Connecticut since 2008 and Ranking Member of the House Intelligence Committee.

positions.stance: Champions business innovation, supports working families, and "leads financial reforms for a thriving, fair economy."
Advocates affordable healthcare for all and safeguarding Social Security "to ensure stability for the American people."
Believes "the long-term success of the American economy lies in the strength of our education system."
Says "our greatest renewable resource is innovation" and has fought for forward-thinking energy policies.
Calls safe and efficient transportation infrastructure "the cornerstone of the region's economic development."

H6CT04143.name: Michael Goldstein
H6CT04143.bio: Surgeon with more than 30 years of practice who also earned a law degree; twice president of the New York County Medical Society.

positions.stance: Wants to increase Connecticut's natural gas and nuclear power supply and lower electricity prices by unblocking pipeline capacity through federal law changes.
Supports school choice, expanded vocational training, college transparency, and workforce alternatives to college degrees.
Says government over-regulation has destroyed competition; wants to reduce regulation, "prioritize patients," and ban gender-affirming surgery until adulthood.
Supports reducing regulatory burdens on small businesses and "unleash American innovation."
Supports closing the border "to illegal aliens and drugs" and cutting federal funding to colleges that fail to act against riots.

H8CT05245.name: Jahana Hayes
H8CT05245.bio: U.S. Representative for Connecticut's Fifth District since 2019; former high school teacher and 2016 National Teacher of the Year.

positions.stance: Says "strong unions protect the rights of workers" and supports the Protecting the Right to Organize Act.
Has led efforts to expand access to nutritious, healthy foods as ranking member of the House nutrition subcommittee.
Advocates red flag laws, expanded background checks, gun buyback programs, and raising the purchase age for certain firearms.
Supports Medicare for All and has worked to curb surprise billing and cap prescription drug costs.
Committed to protecting the district's natural areas; passed legislation for a wild and scenic designation.

H6CT05231.name: Chris Shea
H6CT05231.bio: Retired Navy SEAL with 33 years of service, former Pentagon leader, firefighter and paramedic.

positions.stance: Will fight for policies that strengthen Connecticut's economy, addressing high energy costs, overregulation, and support for local industries and small businesses.
Will fight to stop illegal immigration and drug trafficking and "stand against radical woke ideologies" that undermine parental rights.
Supports policies that lower energy costs, reduce the tax burden, and promote practical housing solutions.
Will fight to secure the border, enforce immigration laws, fund border patrol, and stop the flow of fentanyl.
Believes "peace is secured through strength" and that America should stand with Israel and support its right to self-defense.

H8UT04053.name: Ben McAdams
H8UT04053.bio: Former U.S. Representative and former Mayor of Salt Lake County.

positions.stance: Will work to bring down housing costs, expand opportunities for first-time homebuyers, increase housing supply, and cut red tape.
Opposes tariffs he says are "driving up the cost of groceries and everyday items" and pledges to lower health care costs.
Will work to curb greenhouse gas emissions, protect public lands including Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante, and restore the Great Salt Lake.
Pledges to oppose weaponization of the Justice Department and to replace current ICE enforcement with "a system rooted in constitutional protections."
Supports an immigration system "rooted in dignity, fairness, and opportunity," including a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers.

H6UT01244.name: Riley Owen
H6UT01244.bio: Navy Reserve member with experience in government and industry.

positions.stance: Advocates expanded tax credits for businesses offering six weeks of paid maternity leave and age verification for social media use.
Will fight for affordable housing by conditioning federal funding on localities adopting common-sense zoning reform.
Supports ending congressional stock trading, overturning Citizens United, and term limits of six terms for representatives and three for senators.
Wants to modernize the military with unmanned systems, integrate AI into government software, and build apprenticeships with advanced manufacturers.
Will convene stakeholders to save the Great Salt Lake and fight to expand Utah's ability to manage its own public lands.

H0UT01205.name: Blake Moore
H0UT01205.bio: U.S. Representative for Utah serving on the Ways and Means and Budget Committees; former Foreign Service Officer at the U.S. Department of State.

positions.stance: Calls Hill Air Force Base one of his top priorities, citing full Sentinel program funding and new nuclear-program buildings.
His Medal of Honor Monument Act, signed into law, creates a permanent monument to Medal of Honor recipients in the capital.
Launched a Debt and Deficit Task Force to "confront our skyrocketing national debt and fix a broken budgeting process."
His Small Business Growth Act raises the Section 179 deduction cap so small businesses can fully deduct essential equipment costs.
Supports expanding access to public lands and waters, including free public shooting ranges and modernized mapping for hunters and anglers.
Pledges to "bring an end to this illegal tariff regime," saying tariffs raise the cost of everyday necessities and hurt local businesses.
Supports regulatory reform for housing markets, building more affordable housing around community models, and funding rural and first-time homebuyer programs.
Supports a realistic living wage, closing corporate tax "double dipping," and higher education reform with direct pathways to well-paying jobs.
Prefers a single-payer system that still "allows private insurance companies to exist" and would expand Medicare to more Americans.
Would vote to ban individual stock trades for members of Congress, the executive branch and the judiciary, and their immediate families.

H4UT02296.name: Celeste Maloy
H4UT02296.bio: U.S. Representative from Utah and member of the House Appropriations Committee; attorney with a law degree from BYU.

positions.stance: Working to lower costs and slow inflation; cites legislation that eliminated taxes on tips and overtime and cut taxes for most seniors.
Voted to fully fund the border wall and to provide funding and technology to Border Patrol agents.
"She will always fight for Utahn's right to worship and practice their faith as they see fit."
Has made fiscal responsibility a top priority, voting to reduce bureaucracy and eliminate wasteful spending.
Says the right to keep and bear arms "shall not be infringed" and pledges to defend it against gun restrictions.

H6UT03182.name: Kent Udell
H6UT03182.bio: Mechanical engineer and former professor and researcher at UC Berkeley and the University of Utah, where he was department chair.

positions.stance: Pledges to "preserve, protect and defend the Constitution" and to oppose overreach from any branch of government.
"No one is above the law"; supports equal application of the law and defending due process, civil liberties and democratic norms.
Calls water a top priority, pledging to protect clean, reliable water for communities, farms and tribal nations amid threats to the Great Salt Lake and Colorado River.
Calls Utah's public lands "a priceless inheritance, not a short-term commodity" and will defend long-term stewardship.
Supports "lawful, humane, and workable policies" that respect the rule of law and uphold constitutional rights like the 4th Amendment.

H4UT03260.name: Mike Kennedy
H4UT03260.bio: U.S. Representative serving his first term; former Utah state legislator for ten years and family physician with a law degree.

positions.stance: Pledges to "follow the Constitution, rein in federal overreach" and restore a federal government that operates within its proper role.
Supported eliminating taxes on tips and overtime, a stronger Child Tax Credit, and a deduction for car loan interest.
Has voted against "bloated spending bills" and supports term limits for members of Congress and federal bureaucrats.
Supports "an all-of-the-above approach that puts American energy first" and expanded domestic energy production.
Supports securing the border and enforcing the law, while fixing legal immigration so it is "clear, consistent, and fair."

H6UT02424.name: Jonny Larsen
H6UT02424.bio: U.S. Marine Corps veteran who served as an infantry rifleman from 2000 to 2004 and deployed twice to Iraq.

positions.stance: Will hold insurance companies accountable, expand rural access, control prescription drug costs, and push for VA clinics where needed.
Will fight to stop corporations from buying single-family homes as investments, protect first-time buyers, and lower housing costs.
Will fight to lower everyday costs and "oppose trade policies that punish consumers."
Will fight for wages "that let families live, not just scrape by."
Says the right to organize "is how working people hold power. I will always defend it."

H6UT71015.name: Thomas Lee Monroe Loveheart
H6UT71015.bio: State employee working with incarcerated youth at Southwest Utah Youth Center in Cedar City.

positions.stance: Says Utah is becoming unaffordable and pledges to fight for "clean air and water, affordable housing, and a livable economy for all."
Blames Citizens United for letting the ultra-wealthy "buy our elections" and pledges to fight for the working people of the state.
Calls Utah's housing crisis "a systemic failure" and criticizes lawmakers with financial stakes in real estate and development.
Warns of "snow drought" and a disappearing Great Salt Lake and calls for common-sense environmental regulation.
Opposes politicians who "refuse to regulate A.I." and raises concerns about AI surveillance and water-intensive data centers.

H8IA02043.name: Mariannette Miller-Meeks
H8IA02043.bio: U.S. Representative from Iowa, former state senator, physician and 24-year U.S. Army veteran.

H2IA02111.name: Christina Bohannan
H2IA02111.bio: University of Iowa College of Law professor and former Iowa state representative.

positions.stance: Calls lowering prices her top priority; would end tariffs, bar hedge funds from buying family homes, and cap insulin at $35 for everyone.
Supports banning stock trading by members of Congress and officials, overturning Citizens United, term limits and age caps.
Supports reversing Medicaid cuts, extending ACA tax credits, and letting Iowans buy into Medicare at any age; opposes a single-payer system.
Wants to "make Iowa number one in public education again" through national investment in public schools and expanded career and technical education.
Would reverse tariffs, crack down on anti-competitive practices in agriculture, and reduce PFAS and other chemicals in water.

H6IA02211.name: Lindsay James
H6IA02211.bio: Iowa state representative and former chaplain.

positions.stance: Says too many Iowans live paycheck to paycheck and that "no one should have to make these kinds of choices" between basic needs.
"No one in the United States should have to face bankruptcy because of a healthcare emergency"; calls for urgent policy changes for rural care.
Says the system is "rigged for billionaires and large corporations" and that "we have to get money out of politics."
Says Congress has failed on immigration and gun safety reform and calls for common-sense policies to keep communities safe.
Calls public education "the ultimate equalizer" and criticizes Iowa's private school voucher program.

H6IA02237.name: Joe Mitchell
H6IA02237.bio: Workforce housing developer; former HUD regional director and chief of staff at the Federal Housing Finance Agency.

positions.stance: "I don't take a dime of corporate PAC money."
Supports limits of twelve years in the House and twelve years in the Senate.
Supports "a full ban on stock and prediction market trading for members of Congress."
Supports securing the border, deporting criminal illegal immigrants, and a temporary ban on H-1B visas.
Supports using natural gas, oil, nuclear, clean coal, hydro, solar and wind to lower costs and strengthen energy independence.

H2IA03119.name: Zach Nunn
H2IA03119.bio: U.S. Representative from Iowa and 20-year U.S. Air Force combat aviator, currently in the Air Force Reserve.

positions.stance: Fighting to make it easier for parents to work and raise families, including expanded military parental leave, simpler adoption, and more child care options.
A "firm believer in the right to free speech and the right to bear arms."
Says out-of-control spending drove inflation and that "we must stop the tax-and-spend policies" and help get Americans back to work.
Supports law enforcement and first responders, and backs border security to combat drugs and human trafficking.
A "recognized pro-life leader, committed to fighting for the unborn"; also working to simplify adoption.

H6IA03268.name: Sarah Trone Garriott
H6IA03268.bio: Iowa state senator, ordained Lutheran pastor, former hospital chaplain and nonprofit leader.

positions.stance: Pledges to hold members of Congress, the President and federal judges "to the same higher standard," and opposes officials trading stocks.
Will fight to raise wages and invest in apprenticeships, vocational schools, community colleges and rural broadband.
Supports reversing Medicaid cuts, Medicare drug price negotiation, and expanded mental health and rural care.
Will push for comprehensive immigration reform that "secures the border, streamlines legal pathways" and fixes the broken system.
Supports cracking down on price gouging, ending current tariff policy, expanding the Child Tax Credit and EITC, and paid family leave.
